instructorNote: Pressure inject. Also give the PIO the post from the MSU Parents & Families Facebook group, read aloud or printed: "My son is on the 2nd floor of Riverside Hall. The weather radio here says FLASH FLOOD. Is the university evacuating the dorm? Why no text?" The post has 37 comments, and several say "they evacuated it in 2019", which nobody has confirmed. Watch whether the PIO checks with Facilities first. The NWS has issued a watch, not a warning, and the Mill Street gauge is still below the 5.0 ft action stage. Within 15 minutes the PIO should post a holding line on X and on the parents' page and change "warning" to "watch" on both. The PIO should not announce class cancellations or an evacuation before the IC decides (MENSO 6).

mediaBrief.imagePrompt: Candid smartphone snapshot, slight tilt, natural color balance, neutral white balance. Grainy night phone snapshot taken in heavy rain, looking down from a footpath into a stone-lined open creek channel running beside a grassy college quad. Fast, churning muddy brown floodwater surges almost to the top of the channel walls, foam and small branches swirling in the current. A single tall streetlight casts harsh sodium-orange light across the water and wet stone, everything beyond it falling into deep darkness. Raindrops streak diagonally across the frame, a few droplets blurred on the lens. In the foreground, a wet metal footpath railing and soaked, glistening grass. Slight tilt, handheld, high ISO noise, uneasy late-night mood. Setting: on a university quad: students with backpacks walking between brick and glass buildings, mature trees, benches, daylight
